parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The unit has one file, src/application/order-service.ts, with one class, OrderService. It handles one concern: the order and product use cases. Its public methods are addProduct, placeOrder, progressOrder, cancelOrder, listOrders and listProducts. Each one works the same way: load data through the injected ProductRepository or OrderRepository, call a domain method (reserve, release, advanceTo, cancel), then save. All errors are DomainError. Order state changes stay in the domain (order.advanceTo, order.cancel), and stock changes stay in Product (reserve, release), so the service doesn't change entity state directly.

There is one small inconsistency. placeOrder looks up each product itself and throws DomainError("PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND", ...). The private helper requireProduct does the same thing with the same error code and message, and cancelOrder uses that helper. So the not-found check exists in two places in one file. The in-line availability check (item.quantity > product.availableStock) may repeat a check inside Product.reserve. The code comment says it is deliberate: every line is checked before any stock is reserved. The source of Product isn't provided, so I can't confirm whether it is a duplicate. normaliseItems validates order lines at the application layer. Whether Order repeats that check can't be confirmed either.

These are small, local issues inside one file. The module doesn't split into unrelated concerns and doesn't bypass its domain abstractions, so overall it meets the rubric.
